I've seen it time and time again - teams struggling to decide between Redshift Spectrum and Athena for querying S3 data. The truth is, choosing the right tool can save you thousands of dollars in query costs.

To query S3 directly with Redshift Spectrum, use the `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE` statement to define your schema. 
This approach is ideal for large-scale data warehousing workloads.
For ad-hoc queries, Amazon Athena is a better choice - simply use the `START QUERY EXECUTION` API to run SQL queries on your S3 data.
When dealing with complex queries, consider using Redshift Spectrum with `UNLOAD` command to optimize performance.
